claims.text:
20. isolation-forest

Target / packet: ai-isolation-forest · C2. Prerequisites: ai:decision-tree-splits.

Nearest / distinct payoff: decision-tree-splits → which-question-splits. A split tree need not classify labels; these isolation partitions use depth and a declared anomaly score with a short-path countercase.

Finite primary model: Points[0,1,2,10]. Tree A splits x<6 then left x<.5 then x<1.5: depth 10=1, depth 1=3. Tree B root x<.5, then right x<6, then left x<1.5: depth 10=2, depth 1=3. Mean paths 1.5 vs 3; with declared normalizer c=2, scores 2^(-path/c)≈.594604 vs.353553.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Point 0 has depth 2 in tree A but 1 in tree B; one short path is not proof of anomaly. These are declared isolation trees, not randomly fitted forest or an empirical detector.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict which point gets higher score; recall why averaging two paths differs from trusting one split.

Required observable evidence: Show only 4 points and stepwise tree path; score formula/normalizer explicit, not claimed exact sklearn forest score.

Source obligation: [scikit-learn Isolation Forest description](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/outlier_detection.htmlisolation-forest), acquired body. Local two fixed trees and score normalizer2 are declared teaching parameters; do not call them a reproduced fitted sklearn forest or its full scoring implementation.
